item.text:
**Bottom line**  
Mixed, leaning mildly positive on oversight and local-accountability institutions, but weak on courts/legislatures specifically. The strongest 2024 evidence is Biden-era DOJ and administrative oversight of local policing and civilian-harm review; the main counterevidence is a coercive protest-policing environment and incomplete follow-through on some oversight channels.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [GAO says DOD and State built civilian-harm response processes, with DOD implementing all CHMR-AP objectives by Dec. 16, 2024](https://files.gao.gov/reports/GAO-25-107077/index.html) | U.S. Government Accountability Office | 2025-04-24 | https://files.gao.gov/reports/GAO-25-107077/index.html | A congressional audit found the administration had created formal processes to respond to civilian-harm reports and that DOD was in the final phases of implementing the full civilian-harm mitigation plan by late 2024. This is the clearest evidence of strengthening oversight infrastructure. | 4B.4; also 3B.7 |
| [DOJ finds Phoenix police violated civil rights](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/justice-department-finds-civil-rights-violations-phoenix-police-department-and-city-phoenix) | U.S. Department of Justice | 2024-06-13 | https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/justice-department-finds-civil-rights-violations-phoenix-police-department-and-city-phoenix | Biden’s DOJ publicly investigated and condemned unconstitutional policing by a local government, showing federal oversight of a subordinate institution rather than shielding it from scrutiny. | 4B.4; also 3B.8, 3B.9 |
| [DOJ announces Louisville policing consent decree](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/speech/assistant-attorney-general-kristen-clarke-delivers-remarks-announcing-consent-decree) | U.S. Department of Justice | 2024-12-12 | https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/speech/assistant-attorney-general-kristen-clarke-delivers-remarks-announcing-consent-decree | DOJ reached a court-enforceable reform decree after finding violations in Louisville, which is direct evidence of using oversight and judicially supervised remedies to constrain a local government. | 4B.4; also 3B.8, 3B.9 |
| [DOD issues civilian-harm mitigation instruction](https://www.defense.gov/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/3624268/dod-issues-civilian-harm-mitigation-response-instruction/) | U.S. Department of Defense | 2024-02-13 | https://www.defense.gov/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/3624268/dod-issues-civilian-harm-mitigation-response-instruction/ | DOD formalized oversight, incident review, training, and senior civilian supervision for civilian-harm mitigation. This is internal institutional strengthening, though not as strong as independent external oversight. | 4B.4; also 3B.7 |
| [GAO says civilian-harm oversight was still incomplete and not fully independent](https://files.gao.gov/reports/GAO-25-107077/index.html) | U.S. Government Accountability Office | 2025-04-24 | https://files.gao.gov/reports/GAO-25-107077/index.html | The same audit found CHIRG would not accept non-government reports and that State had not completed investigations into credible reports by Dec. 2024. That weakens the case for robust, independent oversight. | 4B.4; also 3B.7 |
| [Reuters: police were advised to avoid mass arrests, then came the US campus protests](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/police-were-advised-to-avoid-mass-arrests-then-came-the-us-campus-protests-3433913) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-05-10 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/police-were-advised-to-avoid-mass-arrests-then-came-the-us-campus-protests-3433913 | This is the strongest counterexample in the 2024 record: a large protest wave met mass arrests despite advice to avoid that approach, suggesting a coercive local-enforcement climate rather than consistently strengthening rights-protective institutions. | 4B.4; also 3B.8, 3B.9 |
| [Washington Post: more than 2,000 campus arrests in a short span](https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/interactive/2024/university-antiwar-campus-protests-arrests-data/?itid=lk_fullstory&itid=lk_inline_manual_26&itid=lk_inline_manual_5) | The Washington Post | 2024-05-03 | https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/interactive/2024/university-antiwar-campus-protests-arrests-data/?itid=lk_fullstory&itid=lk_inline_manual_26&itid=lk_inline_manual_5 | The protest environment featured riot-police tactics, tear gas, tasers, and stun grenades at scale. That undercuts a broad claim that the administration reliably encouraged independent civil-society monitoring or noncoercive local governance. | 4B.4; also 3B.8, 3B.9 |

**Search gap**  
I found no strong 2024 evidence of Biden actively strengthening independent courts or legislatures when they constrained him. The best support for 4B.4 is narrower: DOJ-led accountability for local police, formal civilian-harm oversight, and audit-body scrutiny. The record is much thinner on affirmative court- or legislature-strengthening actions.
